chunks: And it is narrated from ʿAbdullāh ibn Jaʿfar al-Ḥimyarī, who said:

I asked him, peace be upon him, in a letter, about a man who bought a camel, a cow, a sheep, or something else for sacrificial animals or otherwise. Then, when he slaughtered it, he found in its belly a pouch containing dirhams, dinars, jewels, or other such benefits. To whom does that belong, and how should he deal with it?
So he, peace be upon him, wrote: “Inform the seller about it. If he does not recognize it, then the thing is yours; Allah has provided it to you.”

key_terms.جَزُورًا: a camel purchased and then slaughtered
key_terms.دَرَاهِمُ: silver coins found in the pouch
key_terms.دَنَانِيرُ: gold coins found in the pouch
key_terms.رَزَقَكَ: Allah has provided it to you as sustenance
key_terms.صُرَّةً: a tied pouch or bundle found inside the animal
key_terms.عَرِّفْهَا: inform the seller about it and identify the found item to him

ai.seo_question: What should someone do if money or valuables are found inside an animal after buying and slaughtering it?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about valuable property found inside a purchased animal after slaughter. The Imam عليه السلام instructs that the seller should first be informed; if the seller does not recognize it, the finder may keep it as provision granted by Allah.
